mistakes.feedback_sk: Zápach zacítila až potom, preto Past Simple: „noticed“. Past Perfect patrí k skoršiemu deju.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Zápach ucítila až potom, proto Past Simple: „noticed“. Past Perfect patří k dřívějšímu ději.
mistakes.feedback_en: She noticed the smell later, so use Past Simple “noticed”; Past Perfect is for the earlier action.

mistakes.text: The fish already scattered when she noticed the smell.

mistakes.feedback_sk: Ryby sa rozpŕchli skôr, ako zacítila zápach, preto Past Perfect: „had already scattered“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Ryby se rozprchly dřív, než ucítila zápach, proto Past Perfect: „had already scattered“.
mistakes.feedback_en: The fish scattered before she noticed the smell, so use Past Perfect: “had already scattered”.

mistakes.feedback_sk: „Notice“ je krátky jednorazový dej, v Past Continuous neznie prirodzene: „noticed“.

mistakes.feedback_en: “Notice” is a short, one-off action, so it doesn't go in Past Continuous: “noticed”.
